The retrosynthetic step would break the S-N bond to give amine and sulfonyl chloride. The template's retro_smarts_template shows reactants (precursors) on left side? Actually retro_smarts_template is the retrosynthetic transformation: product -> precursors. In the result, we have fields: retro_smarts_template, canonical_smarts_template, mapped_rxn (which is forward? It seems mapped_rxn is forward reaction SMILES with mapping). We need to return mapped_rxn associated with the template that reproduces the reaction. So we need to pick appropriate template. Look at first entry reaction_id 758105. Its mapped_rxn: '[CH3:1][S:2](=[O:3])(=[O:4])Cl.Cl.[NH2:5][CH2:9][CH2:10][Cl:11].N[CH2:6][CH2:7][Cl:8].CCN(CC)CC.ClCCl.C1CCOC1>>[CH3:1][S:2](=[O:3])(=[O:4])[N:5]([CH2:6][CH2:7][Cl:8])[CH2:9][CH2:10][Cl:11]'

That seems to involve sulfonyl chloride (Cl attached to S) and amine (N...). The product is sulfonamide with N attached to S and also other substituents. This looks like sulfonamide formation. So this template likely correct.

We need template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). The result includes reaction_id but not template_id. The field maybe "template_id"? Not present. Might be template_id is separate but not shown. However we can assume template_id is reaction_id? The prompt says "template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash)". In search results, likely there is a field "template_id". But not present. Could be that "reaction_id" is the template_id. We'll use reaction_id.
